note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Acute left-sided headache waking patient from sleep this morning; differential discussed as tension-type headache versus migraine.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided headache that woke patient at ~05:30 this morning; still present at time of consult.
- Onset/duration/progression: Sudden onset this morning; woke patient early; headache described as more severe than his usual headaches.
- Characteristics/associated symptoms:
  - Predominantly left-sided pain (patient reports prior headaches were more frontal and bilateral).
  - Mild photophobia (lights make eyes a little sore).
  - Initial dizziness on waking that has since resolved.
  - No nausea (patient states "not really").
  - No neck stiffness, no fever.
  - Headache initially a little worse on lying down but overall feels better when lying down.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No vomiting, no neck stiffness, no fever.
  - No current suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts.
  - No known family history of migraine; mother has anxiety.
- Past medical history and medications:
  - History of anxiety for ~2 years.
  - Currently taking sertraline — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Took paracetamol this morning for the headache — dose/route/frequency not documented; reported no benefit.
  - No other medical illnesses reported.
- Allergies:
  - Patient reports no known medication allergies.
- Social history and preventive care:
  - Lives with partner.
  - Non-smoker.
  - Has a cat.
  - Exercises (running) approximately three times per week.
  - Diet described as "OK" (not unhealthy).
  - Recent increased work-related stress and late nights for ~2 months.

Examination:
- Vitals: none documented.
- Physical examination findings: no physical examination performed during this remote consultation.

Impression:
- Working differential: tension-type headache vs migraine.

Plan:
- Pharmacologic:
  - Start ibuprofen — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Continue paracetamol if desired (patient has already taken paracetamol today with no benefit).
- Advice and non-pharmacologic measures:
  - Recommend considering short-term time off work (suggested up to one week self-certified) to reduce stress.
  - Explore local counseling service; clinician will include referral link for patient self-referral.
  - Sleep hygiene: aim for 7–8 hours sleep per night.
  - Hydration: aim for 1.5–2.0 liters of fluids daily (excluding coffee/tea).
- Safety netting and follow-up:
  - Follow-up appointment arranged in one week with same service (with clinician or another doctor).
  - If symptoms worsen or patient becomes concerned, advised to contact clinic earlier for reassessment.
  - If no improvement after initial measures, clinician may arrange blood tests or further investigations.
  - Clinician will add a link to headache danger signs in the notes for patient review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature) are not documented.
  - No neurological or head/neck physical examination performed or documented.
  - Medication details incomplete: sertraline dose/route/frequency not documented; ibuprofen dose/route/frequency not documented; paracetamol dose not documented.
  - No formal medication reconciliation or allergy verification beyond patient report.
  - No baseline investigations (e.g., blood tests) performed or documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Minor name inconsistencies noted in the dialogue (patient initially referred to as "Atan"/"Anthony" but later gives name as Ayrton Warren) — not relevant to clinical content but recorded.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall clear and audible with minor pauses and conversational interruptions; clinical information adequately captured.
